- Model consistently overestimates prices in the short term (first 5–10 days) after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is negative or volatile.  
- When sentiment turns sharply negative (e.g., -0.50 or below), model tends to overreact with large downward forecasts — but often misses the magnitude of the drop.  
- Model underestimates the speed of mean reversion after peaks; true price often falls faster than forecasted, especially in the 10–20 day window.  
- Forecasts show persistent bias toward higher prices when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive — model fails to adjust downward when sentiment turns negative.  
- Overshoots after spikes are common in model’s 15–30 day horizon — true price often corrects more aggressively than forecasted, especially if sentiment is negative.  
- Model underestimates the impact of sentiment swings on price — when sentiment shifts from negative to neutral, model doesn’t fully adjust upward.  
- Forecasts tend to be too optimistic in the 20–30 day horizon, especially when sentiment is weak or negative — true price often declines more than forecasted.  
- Model fails to capture sentiment-driven volatility — when sentiment is volatile (e.g., alternating +0.37 and -0.50), price corrections are more abrupt than forecasted.
